sovereign_country.strategic_role: 拉美西语近岸软件研发外包与数字客服中心

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Accounts Receivable Factoring and Cross-Border Reverse Factoring

meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: Colombia (National Unitary Jurisdiction; no sub-state tax distinction)
meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (Romano-Germanic) based on the Constitution of 1991, the Commercial Code (Decree 410/1971), and the SAS Statute (Law 1258 of 2008), with modern regulatory influence from U.S. corporate and AML practice.
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Colombia–United States Trade Promotion Agreement (in force 2012; Financial Services Chapter applicable)
Andean Community (CAN) regulatory framework with Peru and Ecuador

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law 526/1999 (UIAF creation); Law 1121/2006 (AML/CFT framework); Decree 830/2021 (SAGRILAFT / SARLAFT for supervised and non-supervised sectors); DIAN Resolution 164/2022, as amended by Resolution 83/2023 (Registro Único de Beneficiarios Finales – RUBF); Superfinanciera Circular 008/2022 and Circular 061/2007 for financial-risk companies; Law 1231/2008 (transferable factoring instruments, 'factura electrónica de venta'); Decree 477/2022 (factoring and confirming regulatory regime); Civil and Commercial Code provisions on corporate control (Articles 260–268 C. Co.).

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Homonymy (Certificado de Homonimia) for the proposed SAS corporate name
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Cámara de Comercio of the registered office jurisdiction (e.g., Cámara de Comercio de Bogotá)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (only required if used abroad; for domestic incorporation it is an internal registry certificate)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Private incorporation document or public deed of incorporation of the S.A.S., including bylaws, corporate purpose, capital allocation, and legal representative appointment
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary Public (reconocimiento de firma) or shareholders before the Chamber of Commerce online registration tool
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (if executed abroad for corporate shareholders) OR Consular Legalization (for non-Hague jurisdictions)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Power of Attorney from each foreign shareholder or corporate parent in favor of a Colombian attorney-in-fact or the legal representative
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary Public of the shareholder's domicile (foreign) / Notary Public in Colombia (domestic execution)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (Convention of 5 October 1961) OR Consular Legalization for origin countries not party to the Convention

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of shareholder passport or corporate parent's certificate of incorporation and good standing
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Passport authority / Companies Registry of the foreign jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization, plus sworn official translation into Spanish by a Colombian Ministry-certified translator

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: UBO declaration and due diligence package under DIAN Resolution 164/2022 (RUBF Form) and SAGRILAFT onboarding file
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Legal representative, public accountant, and authorized compliance officer
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Domestic notarization of signature; no apostille required for internal registry filing

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all shareholders, legal representatives, directors, and ultimate beneficial owners against the OFAC SDN List, UN Security Council Consolidated List, EU Consolidated List, Colombia's Superfinanciera 'Lista de Agentes del Mercado,' Procuraduría sanction records, and UIAF typology advisories; implementation of risk-based CDD/EDD under Decree 830/2021 (SAGRILAFT) and Circular 061/2007, including ongoing monitoring of wire-transfer counterparties in the factoring chain and annual reporting to UIAF under the SARO reporting rubric; for cross-border SWIFT Payments, additional CFIUS-style counterparty review and Banco de la República foreign-exchange formalities must accompany enhanced due diligence.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registro Único Empresarial (RUES) – https://www.rues.org.co; name reservation executed through the online 'Trámites en Línea' of the local Cámara de Comercio (e.g., Cámara de Comercio de Bogotá).
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Corporate denominations must be expressed in Spanish alphabetic characters; foreign-language terms are admitted if transliterated into Latin script and not likely to confuse the public regarding the entity's nature or nationality; all names must include the legal type suffix 'Sociedad por Acciones Simplificada' or the abbreviation 'S.A.S.'; trademark-sensitive names require prior written authorization from the Superintendencia de Industria y Comercio (SIC).
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Factoring (only permissible if purely descriptive and the entity does not capture public deposits; may trigger heightened SIC and Superintendencia financiera scrutiny)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Name reservations are not extendable; a new reservation request must be filed at the Chamber of Commerce after expiry. Upon rejection, the applicant may file a 'recurso de reposición' with the Cámara de Comercio and, in subsidiary form, a 'recurso de apelación' with the Superintendencia de Industria y Comercio (SIC), within ten (10) business days from notification. Alternatively, the applicant may obtain a written authorization or disassociation letter from the affected entity when the rejection is based on identical, similar, or protected denominations. The SIC appellate decision issues within thirty (30) business days of filing; if the appeal fails, a completely new name inquiry must be initiated.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Partially permitted: the S.A.S. must register a physical address for service of process in the municipality of incorporation. Virtual-office providers are acceptable if they supply a physical local address that remains accessible during business hours and accept judicial and administrative notifications; a P.O. Box or address without a physical reception will be rejected by the Cámara de Comercio. For the factoring model, a contractually designated 'avenida procesal' is recommended, and the legal representative's registered residence must be verifiable.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: ≈35% probability of an unannounced verification visit ('visita de verificación') by the Cámara de Comercio or the Superintendencia de Sociedades within the first 24 months of registration. The likelihood rises to ≈60% if SWIFT cross-border wires or escrow funding volumes exceed USD 500,000 in the first 90 days of operations, given the Subject-to-Control tier and the 'Medium_Risk_Enhanced' AML classification of trade payables factoring.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Name clearance application and certificate of homonymy (Certificado de Homonimia)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Cámara de Comercio (e.g., Cámara de Comercio de Bogotá) – statutory tariff of approx. COP 40,000
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Chamber of Commerce published tariff schedule for registry certificates

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Incorporation registration fee (derechos de inscripción de la matrícula mercantil) for the S.A.S.
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Cámara de Comercio – tier tariff based on declared assets (approx. COP 480,000 for mid-range capital)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Impuesto de registro (registration tax) over subscribed capital
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Departamento (Provincial Treasury) through the Cámara de Comercio collection window – 0.7% of registered capital (assumed capital of USD 20,000)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarial fees for signature recognition (reconocimiento de firma) and document protocolization if executed before a notary
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Notary Public (Superintendencia de Notariado y Registro tariff regime)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory notary tariff schedule (approx. COP 320,000 for up to 10 pages)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Hague Apostille / Consular Legalization of foreign incorporation documents and powers of attorney (per document)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Colombian Ministry of Foreign Affairs (SIA digital apostille platform) or foreign competent authority
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Ministry of Foreign Affairs fee resolution; market rate

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Official Spanish translation of non-Spanish documents (per page)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Colombian Ministry of Foreign Affairs-certified official translator (traductor oficial)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark for certified translation; tariff per page

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registered agent and virtual office service with physical service-of-process address
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Private corporate-service provider (virtual office licensed in Colombia)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Annual market benchmark for commercial domicile and notification reception

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: UBO (RUBF) registration and filing support with DIAN
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Professional fee of local compliance counsel; DIAN does not levy a registration fee
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark flat fee; DIAN Resolution 164/2022 online filing

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: SAGRILAFT initial AML/CFT risk manual and implementation (factoring line of business)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Local AML/CFT compliance consultant or legal advisor
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark fixed fee for a 'Medium_Risk_Enhanced' factoring S.A.S. under Decree 830/2021

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Legal opinion on factoring statutory authorization and compliance (Law 1231/2008, Decree 477/2022, financial-capture analysis)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Flat market fee for non-deposit-taking factoring S.A.S. licensing assessment

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Ley 1258 de 2008 (Sociedad por Acciones Simplificada); Código de Comercio arts. 98, 110, 373; Ley 1231 de 2008 on invoice factoring; Decree 1074 of 2015 (mercantile registry).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Cámara de Comercio con jurisdicción en el domicilio social (e.g., Cámara de Comercio de Bogotá) via Ventanilla Única Empresarial (VUE).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Documento Privado de Constitución and Bylaws inscribed in the Registro Único Empresarial (RUE); public deed required if real property is contributed.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-in capital for S.A.S.; capital may be paid in cash or kind in any amount. An escrow account is not required for incorporation, but a dedicated bank account for received factoring receivables and client funds must be opened before operations.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLUTION OF THE FIRST BOARD OF DIRECTORS. The shareholders unanimously resolve: (1) the share capital has been lawfully subscribed and paid in accordance with the S.A.S. bylaws; (2) the registered office and principal place of business is hereby fixed at [address], Bogotá D.C., Colombia, as filed with the Chamber of Commerce; (3) [Name] is appointed as legal representative with broad corporate powers, [Name] as corporate secretary, and [Name] as compliance and AML-factoring officer; (4) the legal representative is authorized to obtain the NIT/RUT, open escrow payment rails, and execute all post-formation registrations before DIAN, the Superintendency of Companies, and civil defense authorities. This resolution is governed by Ley 1258 de 2008.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name availability check and preparation of bylaws
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Log into the Registro Único Empresarial - SIU system and request a certificate of homonymy (certificado de homonimia) for the proposed corporate name 'CO_SAS Trade Finance'. If positive, proceed to draft the private instrument of incorporation and S.A.S. bylaws in Spanish; have each shareholder sign with valid citizenship or passport and appraise any in-kind contributions with a sworn valuation report.
required_dossiers: Completed homonymy application form
Copy of each shareholder’s national ID or passport
Draft private incorporation document and bylaws
Sworn valuation report for in-kind contributions, if any
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is identical or confusingly similar to an existing company, refile using a primary corporate identifier or suffix; appeal the registry denial before the same Cámara de Comercio within five business days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registration with the Chamber of Commerce and issuance of existence certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cámara de Comercio con jurisdicción en el domicilio social
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the signed private incorporation instrument through VUE and pay the applicable registry fee. After review, the Chamber issues the Certificado de Cámara de Comercio (certificate of existence and legal representation), which evidences the legal personality of the S.A.S.
required_dossiers: Signed private incorporation document
Certificate of homonymy
Tax pre-registration number, if assigned
Proof of payment of registry fees
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is queried for minor discrepancies, correct the documents within 10 calendar days via the same VUE portal; if rejected, file a reconsideration petition with the Chamber’s legal department, and then with the Superintendencia de Industria y Comercio if unresolved.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax registration (RUT/NIT) with DIAN and digital signature activation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Dirección de Impuestos y Aduanas Nacionales (DIAN) – online portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After receiving the Chamber certificate, register the S.A.S. in the Registro Único Tributario (RUT) through DIAN’s electronic platform. Obtain the NIT and evidence of characterization as a Sociedad por Acciones Simplificada subject to entity-level income tax; request the electronic signature mechanism for e-invoicing, payroll, and future filings.
required_dossiers: Certificado de existencia y representación legal
Legal representative’s identity document
Proof of registered office address
Bank account details for tax refunds
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If DIAN rejects the RUT template due to mismatches in corporate purpose, restart after aligning the country tax schedule with the approved bylaws; request prórroga (extension) or use a DIAN official as intermediary to correct the data online.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-registration corporate books and beneficial ownership declaration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cámara de Comercio and Superintendencia de Sociedades
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Have the corporate books (share registry, minutes book, and accounting ledgers) stamped and numbered by the Chamber. File the final Beneficiario Final (real beneficiary) report and the initial financial situation of the S.A.S. using the Superintendencia’s online information system (SIRVI). This ensures compliance under the AML/CFT framework.
required_dossiers: Certificado de cámara de comercio
Certificate of corporate book stamping (RUE fee paid)
Form identifying final beneficial owners
Opening balance sheet signed by a certified public accountant
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the platform flags missing data, correct the beneficial owner information and resubmit; late filings may incur fines, remedy by paying the associated fine and filing an actionable corrective document with the Chamber and Superintendencia.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Factoring activity authorization and AML/AML operational registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Superintendencia de Sociedades / Unidad de Información y Análisis Financiero (UIAF)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the expression of non-financial factoring activity (factoring comercial) with the Superintendencia de Sociedades, providing the corporate purpose coding ISIC 6492. Implement and register the SARLAFT (Lavado de Activos y Financiación del Terrorismo) manual; appoint the compliance officer; and open segregated bank accounts for each factoring transaction with SWIFT-wire capability through an authorized commercial bank.
required_dossiers: Certificado de existencia y representación legal
Corporate bylaws and ISIC scope description
AML/SARLAFT compliance manual
Compliance officer acceptance letter
Projected cash flow and risk capital evidence for factoring exposure
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Superintendencia identifies missing required clauses, provide within 15 days a supplemented SARLAFT manual and updated risk classification; in case of a negative response, file an appeal with the same authority, which must resolve within two months.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Superintendencia de Sociedades – Delegatura de Procedimientos Mercantiles (for commercial factoring); Superintendencia Financiera de Colombia if the entity undertakes financial intermediation or public securities.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Autorización de Operación de Factoring (Comercial) / Registro de Actividad de Factoring y SARLAFT

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Autoridad Nacional de Licencias Ambientales (ANLA) / Secretaría Distrital de Ambiente (municipal level)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt – Class III administrative office activity; no full EIA report required. A simple environmental registration (ficha ambiental) may be requested by the municipality for water discharge or if occupied area exceeds 2,000 m².
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater discharge to public sewer must not exceed threshold values of Resolution 0631 of 2015 for non-municipal service activities; volatile organic compounds (VOCs) are below applicable limit values for office use; all electronic waste and ink cartridges must be handled through licensed waste managers.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certificate (Certificado de Seguridad Humana y Protección contra Incendios) issued by Cuerpo Oficial de Bomberos after inspection; structural load certificate for office floors if vault or heavy record-keeping equipment exceed 150 kg/m²; municipal operating permit (SAI) and workplace safety compliance certification from the ARL-occupational risk insurer.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Dirección de Impuestos y Aduanas Nacionales (DIAN) — official portal: www.dian.gov.co; transactional e-services via Muisca (muisca.dian.gov.co)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Foreign entities must obtain a NIT (Número de Identificación Tributaria) through DIAN online pre-registration using a local fiscal representative, providing notarised and apostilled constitutional documents, a local business address, and Chamber of Commerce certification. Upon completion, DIAN assigns the NIT, which also serves as the VAT ID. A Colombian S.A.S. obtains its NIT automatically through the Chamber of Commerce registration process.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation; resident entities are subject to corporate income tax on worldwide income; non-resident shareholders are taxed only on Colombian-source income; no pass-through election is available for S.A.S.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No general check-the-box or pass-through election. Optionally, qualifying small taxpayers may elect the 'Régimen Simple de Tributación' (RST), but this is generally unavailable for financial or factoring activities. Colombian hybrid mismatch rules (Law 2277 of 2022) apply to deny deductions in mismatch arrangements and align tax outcomes with economic substance.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Impuesto al Valor Agregado (IVA) — Value Added Tax
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No turnover threshold for legal entities; every S.A.S. must register as an IVA responsible before commencing taxable activities. Natural persons may qualify as 'non-responsables' only if they are not importers/exporters and gross income does not exceed 3,500 UVT (approximately 147,017,500 COP in 2024).
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory electronic invoicing ('Factura Electrónica de Venta') via DIAN-certified software. Invoices must be transmitted for real-time validation and clearance using CUFE/CUDE codes, with a digital XML, QR code, and DIAN validation status. This applies also to export sales and zero-rated services.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of goods and qualifying services are taxable at 0% VAT with refund rights. Goods exports require legal outflow of the goods from Colombian customs territory to the foreign buyer. Services must be provided to a non-resident, effectively used or exploited outside Colombia, and not linked to Colombian real estate or assets; the exporter must register and comply with DIAN Resolution 316 of 2017. Cross-border factoring/reverse factoring can qualify if the service is wholly consumed abroad, subject to financial-services exclusion rules.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Approved Customs Export Declaration (Declaración de Exportación/DEX)
Transport document (Bill of Lading / Air Waybill / Carta Porte Internacional)
Commercial invoice issued by the exporter
Inward Remittance Certificate from a Colombian foreign-exchange intermediary (certificación de reintegro de divisas)
Proof of foreign payment (SWIFT/bank transfer) and the export contract for services
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: DIAN may review zero-rating claims retroactively for up to five years. If supported documentation for physical export, service delivery abroad, and FX repatriation is incomplete, the taxpayer will be assessed 19% VAT plus monthly interest penalties (approximate current charge 2.3% per month), and an inexact-return penalty up to 200% of the omitted tax. Fraudulent or forged export documentation triggers criminal tax-evasion liability under Law 1762 of 2015, with imprisonment from 4 to 9 years; shareholders and legal representatives may also be held jointly liable.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banco de la República (Central Bank of Colombia) and Superintendencia Financiera de Colombia
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Colombia maintains a liberalized exchange control regime, but the Colombian peso is not fully freely convertible outside the domestic banking system. Current account transactions, including trade settlements and profit remittances, are generally permitted and convertible through authorized FX intermediaries. However, capital account operations, including foreign investment, loans, and factoring-related cross-border flows, require registration with Banco de la República, the filing of foreign exchange declaration declarations (Declaraciones de Cambio), and compliance with quantitative reporting thresholds. Profit remittances require evidence of payment of income tax (impuesto de renta) and documentation of the underlying investment registration. For trade supply chain factoring, conversion of foreign currency proceeds is mandatory and must be channeled through the Colombian foreign exchange market within strict timelines. Non-resident factoring entities are subject to limitations on local onboarding and must act through licensed Colombian financial institutions or branches.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Export proceeds must be repatriated to Colombia within 6 months from the date of export (extendable to 12 months with prior Banco de la República authorization). A minimum of 80% of export proceeds must be converted into Colombian pesos (COP) and sold to the domestic foreign exchange market through an authorized intermediary within the statutory surrender window. The remaining 20% may be held in foreign currency accounts locally or abroad outside the mandatory surrender requirement. For factoring companies, collection of assigned export receivables from foreign debtors must be routed into the Colombian FX market through an authorized bank, and the transaction must be reported on the applicable foreign exchange declaration form (Formulario No. 5, 10, 11, or 12). Failure to comply triggers fines, penal interest, suspension of FX registration, and loss of tax benefits associated with investment or export activity.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account / Operational Account / Foreign Currency Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low-Medium feasibility. Colombia does not recognize foreign electronic money institutions (EMIs) as authorized payment institutions. Digital-only banks and offshore EMIs cannot directly open local bank accounts or process local COP clearing without obtaining a license from the Superintendencia Financiera de Colombia or establishing a local commercial financing company (compañía de financiamiento). However, a foreign EMI may serve as a complementary payment gateway for collecting funds from non-Colombian debtors, provided that all funds are subsequently settled into a Colombian commercial bank account for FX surrender. Direct operation of a Colombian peso wallet or receiving export proceeds in an offshore EMI is not permitted.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence is effectively mandatory for opening a corporate bank account. According to Superintendencia Financiera Circular 008 of 2021, heightened due diligence applies to entities engaged in factoring and non-bank financial activities. The legal representative and ultimate beneficial owner are generally required to attend an in-person interview at the bank's offices in Bogotá, Medellín, or Cali, unless the company qualifies for remote opening under exceptional conditions in which case remote verification may be permitted using a Colombian consulate-validated KYC dossier. In all cases, corporate documents must be notarized, apostilled, and translated into Spanish; for a S.A.S., the sole shareholder may act as legal representative and must present a valid passport and tax registration (RUT). Appointing a Chilean-style 'revisor fiscal' is required when the company's assets exceed 5,000 UVT or when factoring activity represents a significant share of revenue.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unlicensed factoring activity detected: entity does not hold a special authorization from Superintendencia Financiera or is not duly registered in the Factoring Registry managed by Fiducolombia or the National Guarantee Fund.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified Articles of Incorporation of the S.A.S., certified RUT, Superintendencia authorization for factoring under Law 1231 of 2008, due diligence policy manual (Sarlaft), AML compliance officer appointment, sworn statement on beneficial ownership, and audited financial statements.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border payment red flag: high volume of incoming wire transfers from tax havens or transactions involving offshore shell entities.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Detailed counterparty profile (legal registration, economic rationale, underlying invoices), certified copies of underlying trade contracts, KYC files of the assignor and debtor, sanctions screening results (OFAC, EU, Colombian national list), declaration of no shell activity, and audit trail of the commercial transaction.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: FX surrender red flag: foreign currency proceeds are not being converted within the statutory timeframe.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Bank account statements showing FX transactions, foreign exchange declaration forms (Formularios de Declaración de Cambio), export/import contracts, customs documents (DEX/DIO), and a written FX conversion policy mandating that 80% of proceeds are settled within the 6-month period.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: UBO/PEP risk: ultimate beneficial owner holds political exposure or the ownership structure is complex.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Professional UBO registry report, sworn PEP declaration, source-of-wealth report with bank statements and tax returns, notarized explanation of funds, and an independent third-party Enhanced Due Diligence (EDD) report from a recognized risk intelligence provider.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound capital injections must be routed via SWIFT MT103/MT202 to an authorized Colombian commercial bank in COP or foreign currency. Transfers must reach the company's COP account under the company's NIT tax identification number and include the capital contribution purpose code. The transaction must be registered on Banco de la República's foreign exchange declaration forms within 30 calendar days if the contribution qualifies as foreign direct investment (FDI) in an S.A.S. The bank will validate the KYC marginal note on the company's RUT and issue a certificate of retention. To avoid blocking, the sending bank must include the full company corporate name, RUT ID 'CO_SAS', and a clear reference such as 'Capital Contribution / Share Subscription'. Foreign debtors' payments to the factoring account shall be identified with the underlying invoice and the corresponding NIT.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound trade disbursements are cleared using: (a) local COP payments through CENIT or the ACH system for domestic suppliers of trade payables; (b) SWIFT MT103 for cross-border payments of foreign invoices, using proper purpose and dedicated description 'Trade Finance Disbursement'; and (c) commercial letters of credit (import/export L/C) issued by the Colombian bank on behalf of the factoring entity. The bank must verify electronic invoice (CUE) and the underlying factoring contract before release. For reverse factoring, payments must be made to the supplier's local account and immediately recorded as factoring disbursement, with the debtor's repayment later received through MT103 from abroad and converted via the local market.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) on USD/COP contracted with authorized intermediaries, but limited to hedging physical receipts.
Deliverable COP/USD forward contracts through local commercial banks, requiring underlying trade flow.
Cross-currency swaps (CCS) between COP and USD/EUR, for tenor matching borrowing cycles.
FX options (caballos) purchased for downside protection, provided they align with the trade receivable portfolio.
Cancellation of hedging positions via novation or offset, but physical conversion of funds must be conducted through the Colombian FX market.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Renewal of the commercial registration (renovación de la matrícula mercantil)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Local Chamber of Commerce (Cámara de Comercio) with jurisdiction over the registered domicile, under Superintendencia de Industria y Comercio oversight
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually between January 1 and March 31, or the next business day if March 31 falls on a non-working day
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late renewal triggers monetary sanctions and interest; continued non-renewal for the statutory period results in cancellation of the mercantile registration and administrative strike-off, extinguishing the company's operational legal capacity.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 35% (Colombian corporate income tax rate under Law 2277 of 2022, applicable to taxable years 2023 onwards)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No general tax holiday or free-zone regime applies to commercial factoring. The principal preferential mechanism is the additional 25% tax deduction for qualifying investments in scientific research, technological development, and innovation (CTeI). Investment in fixed productive assets and certain green-energy assets may also be deducted under specific rules, but no unconditional statutory tax holiday is available for foreign-owned Colombian S.A.S. entities.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Formulario 210 (Declaración de Renta y Complementarios para personas jurídicas), filed electronically through the DIAN virtual portal (MUISCA/DIAN website) with an electronic signature and digital certificate.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual (with advance income-tax installment calculation accompanying the declaration; the advanced payment is recognized as prepaid CIT for the following tax year).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The annual income tax return is due according to DIAN's official tax calendar, determined by the last two digits of the taxpayer's NIT. For a calendar-year Colombian S.A.S., the return is generally due no later than the September filing window of the immediately following tax year.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxpayer's Colombian tax identification number, verification digit, reason for filing, and fiscal period. The taxable year defaults to the calendar year unless DIAN previously authorized a different fiscal period.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident with a Colombian permanent establishment (PE) must obtain a Colombian NIT before filing and must state that it is acting only through its registered PE. A non-resident without a Colombian PE must not file Form 210 for Colombian-sourced income; the Colombian payer applies final withholding tax on gross amounts.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Identifies the annual taxable period covered by the return, stated as AAAA (e.g., 2025).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The PE must file for the same fiscal year as its head office if the head office does not use a calendar year; however, the PE must calculate Colombian CIT only on Colombian-source income and expenses economically connected to the PE.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 23 — Gross Income from Factoring Operations
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Reports all revenues derived from accounts-receivable factoring and reverse factoring: purchase discount margin, service commissions, late-payment interest, commission for administrative collection, and any recovery of written-off receivables.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include only Colombian-source factoring income, i.e., income where the debtor is resident in Colombia, where the payment obligation arises from commercial operations carried out in Colombia, or where the recourse activity is performed in Colombia. Foreign-source factoring income of a non-resident with no Colombian PE is not declarable.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Reports business expenses attributable to factoring operations: direct operational expenses, financial costs, employee costs, rent, technology and software, administrative expenses, provisions for bad debts (limited to the technical reserve rules), and the CTeI additional deduction.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A PE may deduct only expenses that are economically linked to its Colombian factoring business. Head-office charges must be supported by intercompany agreements and transfer pricing documentation; deductible allocations are limited to the equivalent of services actually performed and are subject to withholding if charged as payments to the head office.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 55 — Net Taxable Income or Tax Loss
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Determines the resulting net taxable income, or a tax loss, after applying prior-year loss carryforwards and permissible deductions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The PE carries forward tax losses for the same maximum 5-year period. A loss carryforward is only permitted when evidenced by audited financial statements and DIAN-recognized accounting; it cannot be used against unrelated non-resident income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 70 — Theoretical Self-Withholding on Dividend Distributions
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Records the net taxable income and the income considered distributed to shareholders during the period. Colombian companies are required to declare and pay the withholding/dividend tax on the actual or deemed distribution of profits to shareholders, including non-resident shareholders.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The non-resident shareholder does not file this box. The Colombian withholding agent (the S.A.S.) must self-withhold and remit the dividend WHT through the monthly withholding form within the tax filing calendar.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing subjects the taxpayer to a penalty of 5% of the tax due, increased monthly (or by fractional month) by 1.5% for late filing, capped at 100% of the tax due. If no tax is due, the penalty is 0.5% of gross income or, when all fields are zero, a fixed amount equal to approximately COP 104,000 (as indexed by UVT). Failure to file also generates default interest at DIAN's effective rate, suspension of the taxpayer's RUT status, and criminal liability if the omission is fraudulent.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 10% on gross dividends paid to non-resident shareholders, applied by the Colombian payer as final withholding tax. Dividends paid from profits previously subjected to 35% Colombian CIT do not generate additional foreign remittance tax beyond this 10% statutory dividend WHT.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke a Colombia double-taxation agreement (DTA), the non-resident shareholder, interest recipient, or royalty recipient must furnish the Colombian withholding agent with a tax residence certificate (TRC) issued by the competent foreign tax authority, generally legalized/apostilled and no older than the taxable year in question. The certificate must identify the beneficial owner and confirm that the recipient is liable to full income tax in its residence country. The Colombian payer then applies the reduced DTA rate during withholding, preserves the TRC and supporting evidence in its records, and reports the treaty-affected payments to DIAN. DIAN may reject treaty relief if the foreign recipient lacks economic substance or is a conduit established solely to obtain treaty benefits under the principal-purpose rule.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory withholding rates: 15% on cross-border royalties for the use of patents, software, trademarks, and similar IP, and 20% on debt interest and financial yields paid to non-residents. Under Colombia's DTAs, royalty WHT is frequently reduced to 10% and interest WHT to 10% or 15%, provided the beneficial-ownership and treaty-linking conditions are met.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: A Colombian S.A.S. is required to prepare and file the Transfer Pricing Declaration, Local File, and Master File when its annual gross income or total gross assets at year-end exceed 100,000 UVTs (approximately COP 4.7 billion for the 2025 fiscal year, adjusted annually by DIAN). Lower mandatory-filing thresholds apply in the case of transactions with individuals or entities situated in designated low-tax or no-tax jurisdictions regardless of the above threshold.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Colombia does not apply a separate Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) code in the Gulf-Council sense. However, Colombian tax law requires the existence of real economic substance for tax-residence, treaty-benefit, and permanent-establishment determinations. A shell S.A.S. used solely to hold factored receivables or to channel cross-border fees without actual personnel, decision-making, and operational activity will be disregarded for Colombian tax purposes under the general anti-avoidance provisions and the economic-substance requirements embedded in Colombian DTA policy. A serial factoring vehicle must maintain full operational substance in Colombia to be treated as Colombian resident and to obtain treaty benefits.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion — False or Omitted Factoring Income
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberately understating gross income from factored receivables, fabricating non-existent trade invoices, treating fake discounts as deductible commissions, or omitting cross-border factoring fees from the Colombian income tax return.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal tax evasion under Article 434 of the Colombian Criminal Code carries imprisonment of 48 to 108 months and a fine equal to 200% to 1,000% of the evaded tax. DIAN additionally imposes corrective-assessments with penalties of up to 200% of the understated tax, default interest, reputational placement on DIAN's public tax-debt registry, and potential cancellation of the RUT.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors, legal representatives, and accountants who sign or cause false declarations may be held personally liable for the tax penalty under the civil-liability rule of Article 793 of the Tax Code; criminal prosecution runs directly against the individuals. Colombian courts may order asset freezes, travel bans, and imprisonment, piercing the ESG structure of the S.A.S. when it is used as a fraud instrument.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating the S.A.S. as a facade entity with no real commercial activity, nominee shareholders, or artificial routing of factoring profits through related shell companies in low-tax jurisdictions solely to avoid Colombian CIT and the 10% dividend WHT.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The artificial structure is disregarded under Colombian anti-abuse doctrine, the S.A.S. is taxed on its worldwide income as a Colombian resident, and the add-back of denied deductions and recharacterized income carries penalties. Additionally, individuals involved in fraud using shell companies may be liable for aggravated fraud and false-reporting criminal offenses under the Criminal Code, with severe fines and imprisonment.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Colombian courts will pierce the corporate veil where the S.A.S. is used to defraud creditors or the tax authority. Directors and shadow directors can be ordered to personally restore diverted funds and pay unpaid taxes, subjected to asset embargoes, named in the UIAF money-laundering risk list, and prohibited from leaving Colombia while criminal investigation is pending.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Unauthorized Factoring Activity / Money Laundering Through Factoring
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Engaging in open, public, or habitual factoring operations without the required statutory license or authorization when the activity constitutes regulated financial business; or laundering criminal proceeds through circular factoring transactions involving shell payers and circular related-party receivables.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Unlicensed financial intermediation is penalized by the Superintendency of Societies and/or the Superintendency of Financial Companies with closure of offices, dissolution of the company, and monetary fines calibrated to illicit gains. Separate money-laundering offenses under Law 599 of 2000 impose substantial imprisonment, fines, and confiscation of assets linked to the laundering scheme.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and compliance officers who knowingly execute unlawful factoring or fail to apply AML/KYC controls are personally liable for criminal fines and long-term imprisonment. The court may issue precautionary measures including travel bans, seizure of personal bank accounts, and disqualification from serving as a director in any Colombian company.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing Misstatement / Abusive Related-Party Factoring Terms
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Setting factoring discounts, commission rates, interest, or collection fees between the Colombian S.A.S. and related non-resident factors at non-arm's-length conditions; failing to file the Transfer Pricing Declaration, Local File, or Master File; or channeling payments to beneficiaries without beneficial ownership.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: DIAN may re-determine the Colombian taxable income using fair arm's-length prices, charge the resulting tax underpayment plus default interest, and impose transfer-pricing penalties equal to up to 2% of the value of unsupported cross-border transactions. Repeated non-compliance triggers aggravated fines and comprehensive tax audits.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Representatives who sign false transfer-pricing documentation are jointly liable for the penalty and may be personally sued for the difference in tax. The individual who authorized or executed the abusive related-party pricing may be named in DIAN's criminal referral; mechanisms include travel bans, confiscation of assets, and imprisonment where the pricing arrangement is proven to be a fraudulent evasion instrument.
